app.name: s3mail
aws.accessDenied: The credentials are right, but they lack a permission. Which one is what the connection test in step 3 says in plain words.
aws.badKeyId: The Access Key ID is wrong. Please check it again in step 1.
aws.badSecret: The Secret Access Key is wrong. Please enter it again in step 1 — a character tends to get lost while copying.
aws.enterKeys: In step 1, under “New credentials”, enter the Access Key ID and Secret and click “Save credentials”.
aws.noConnection: No connection to AWS. Is the internet reachable? A proxy in between?
aws.noCredentials: There are no usable credentials for %s. %s
aws.noRegion: No region is set. Choose one in step 1.
aws.noSuchBucket: There is no such bucket — the name or the region is wrong.
aws.noSuchProfile: The AWS profile “%s” does not exist on this computer. Pick another one — or create it: %s
aws.ssoLoginNeeded: %s signs in through AWS SSO, but there is no valid session. Run “%s” in the terminal once, then click “Load buckets” again.
aws.wrongRegion: The bucket lives in another region. Change the region above.
blocked.buttonTitle: Put this address on the SES suppression list
blocked.confirmText: %s goes onto the AWS account's suppression list. SES will not accept mail to this address any more — not from your colleagues either. You can undo it under “Blocked addresses”.
blocked.explain: The suppression list belongs to the AWS account, not to this mailbox: an address here is blocked for your colleagues too. SES also adds to it by itself, whatever bounces hard.
blocked.title: Blocked addresses
check.delete.hint: s3:DeleteObject is missing. Start with “block deletion”, then everything stays at reading.
check.encryption.clientHint: kms:Decrypt on the key from the SES rule is missing.
check.encryption.none: none — the mail lies in plain text
check.encryption.serverKmsHint: The IAM role needs kms:Decrypt and kms:GenerateDataKey.
check.listBucket.empty: access works, but there is nothing under “%s” yet
check.listBucket.emptyHint: As soon as SES files the first message, it shows up here.
check.listBucket.hintNoPrefix: Either s3:ListBucket is missing, or bucket and region do not belong together.
check.listBucket.hintPrefix: The prefix is the likeliest culprit: an access allowed to see one mailbox only needs it exactly — “%s” with the trailing slash, not the level above. Otherwise s3:ListBucket is missing, or bucket and region do not belong together.
check.sender.hint: Verify the address or the domain in the SES console — otherwise SES refuses to send.
check.sender.noPermission: ses:GetIdentityVerificationAttributes is missing — check the address yourself.
check.sender.none: no address given — replying stays off
check.sharedState.hint: s3:ListBucket on %s%s* is missing. Without it this machine sees the others' changes only after the next compaction.
check.sharedState.ok: the folder for the changes is readable
check.write.hint: s3:PutObject is missing. Without it tags, moving and the trash do not work.
cli.addressFile: The address is also written to: %s
cli.alreadyRunning: s3mail is already running – bringing its window to the front.
cli.bucket: S3 bucket holding the raw mail
cli.from: Sender address for replies (verified in SES)
cli.noBrowser: Do not open a browser automatically
cli.notConfigured: s3mail is not set up yet – wizard: %s
cli.refresh: Seconds between automatic refreshes; 0 turns it off
cli.running: s3mail is running on %s   (Ctrl+C stops it)
cli.setup: Open the wizard even if s3mail is already configured
compose.attachmentTooLarge: “%s” alone already blows past the 10 MB SES accepts.
compose.draftNotRemoved: The message went out – but the draft could not be removed.
compose.sentNotStored: The message went out – but the copy in the sent folder could not be stored.
compose.subject: Subject
compose.tooLarge: The message is larger than the 10 MB SES accepts. Put the file somewhere else – a link is friendlier anyway.
confirm.deleteSome: %d message(s) will be irrevocably deleted from S3.
confirm.emptyTrash: The trash (%d messages) will be irrevocably deleted from S3.
confirm.title: Are you sure?
error.badKeyId: That does not look like an access key ID (it starts with AKIA…).
error.credentialsIncomplete: Both the access key ID and the secret access key are needed.
error.deleteBlocked: Deleting for good is switched off.
error.foreignOrigin: Request from a foreign origin refused
error.noBlocklist: the suppression list is not available
error.noBucket: Without a bucket this cannot work.
error.noKms: This message is encrypted with KMS, but no KMS access is set up.
error.noWizard: the setup wizard is not available
error.notSetUp: s3mail is not set up yet
error.tooLarge: The message is larger than the 10 MB SES accepts.
error.trashOnly: Deleting for good works only from the trash.
lifecycle.on: The trash is emptied automatically after %d days.

nav.new.title: Write a new message (n)

nav.rules.title: Automatic rules
nav.settings.title: Connection, bucket, trash
rules.explain: Applied while indexing new mail: the first matching rule wins. Trash and spam are left alone.
rules.title: Automatic rules
search.placeholder: Search:  invoice · from:customer@x.com · subject:"quote" · after:2026-01-01 · has:attachment · is:unread · tag:important
setup.allowDelete: Allow permanent deletion (out of the trash)
setup.bucket.placeholder: or type the bucket name here
setup.credentials.hint: Stored as an AWS profile in ~/.aws/credentials (readable only by you) — the standard place the AWS tools use as well.
setup.domainVerified: The domain %s is verified — every address below it may send. Enter yours, e.g. firstname@%s.
setup.noBuckets: No buckets found — please type the name directly.
setup.note.noListBuckets: Please type the bucket name directly — this access is not allowed to list the account's buckets (s3:ListAllMyBuckets). That is intended and not a fault.
setup.prefix.hint: Exactly the prefix from your SES rule. Below it s3mail creates spam/, trash/ and archiv/.
setup.readFromAccess: Read from your access: %s. You can adjust it below at any time.
setup.region.hint: The region your bucket lives in and where SES accepts the mail.
setup.sender.hint: or type an address — it has to be verified in SES
setup.step1.hint: s3mail needs access to your AWS account to fetch the mail out of S3. If this computer already has a profile set up, use that one.
setup.step2.hint: The bucket your SES rule writes the mail into. “Load buckets” only works once step 1 is in place — before that s3mail does not know which account to look in.
setup.sub: Fill this in once — after that s3mail starts straight into the mailbox.
setup.title: Set up s3mail
token.file.note: This address is valid as long as s3mail runs. After a restart a new one stands here.
token.title: Token missing
token.what: If the mailbox is open in another tab, reload it there. Otherwise copy the address from the terminal.
token.why: s3mail is only reachable through the address printed in the terminal at startup — it carries a token. Without it, any other user of this computer could reach the mailbox over 127.0.0.1.
